title: Hotpath PR audit heuristics & quick rollback plan
content:
Context:
- Personal scratchpad for reviewing PRs that touch 'hotpaths' (token generation loop, KV cache, batching layer, IO paths).
- Goal: fast triage heuristic to decide if a PR needs full perf run / can be merged to main with mitigations / requires hold + rollback plan.
- This is intentionally terse — keep it as a checklist + minimal repro steps to run locally.

High-level acceptance criteria for hotpath PRs (quick):
1) No new sync/blocking I/O in token-generation loop (look for file reads, sleeps, network calls).
2) KV cache shape/alloc logic unchanged or explicitly bench-compensated.
3) No increase in critical-path allocations > 10% (rough heuristic: small PRs should show no new allocations per-token).
4) Latency p50/p95 for baseline input set unchanged within noise (<= +5% p95) for initial review — if >5% escalate to perf-run.
5) Unit tests + small bench added where behavior is non-trivial.

Quick triage checklist (during PR review):
- Files touched: list them, mark anything that touches runtime/core, batching, scheduler, net/transport.
- Search diff for: "await", "sleep", "fs.read", "grpc", "std::thread::sleep", "synchronized", "synchronized_map" (project language-specific idioms).
- If code touches allocator / buffer resizing / zero-copy paths -> set flag NEEDS_PERF_RUN.
- If change is a pure refactor with identical logic and only variable renames / extraction -> mark SKIP_PERF (but add smoke test).
- Check for added config toggles that are off by default; prefer gating behind feature flag + rollout policy.

Quick local smoke (5-10 mins):
1) Run unit smoke: ./bazel test //runtime:hotpath_smoke --time=60s (or language equivalent).
2) Minimal perf: run microbench harness (bench/hotpath_small.py) with 1000 tokens input x 50 iterations. Record p50/p95 and mem.
3) Regression compare: run baseline commit (git checkout baseline) then run same harness. Quick diff: if p95 delta > +10% -> block.
4) Try concurrently with KV cache warm: run two parallel workers; observe latency tail.

Rollback and canary plan template (fill in on PR if flagged):
- Canary fraction: 1% traffic to new binary/container image; metrics to watch: p50, p95, error-rate, mem- OOMs.
- Feature flag: enable=false by default, staged enable via rollout pipeline.
- Immediate rollback steps: 1) Toggle feature flag off OR 2) revert service deployment to previous image tag (image:org/service:stable-YYYYMMDD) OR 3) re-route to fallback model variant.
- Post-rollback: collect flamegraphs, diagnostic traces for failed window.

Smoke tests to request in PR description (copy to PR checklist):
- small-token-path: 128 tokens, batch size 1, KV cold/warm runs (3 each)
- throughput-path: batch size 8, n_workers 4, 1 minute run — check 99th percentile
- memory-path: sustained stream for 5 minutes looking for steady growth (leak)
- error-injection: simulate partial failure in backing store (return 500s) and ensure graceful degradation/fallback

Observability hooks to verify (quick grep):
- Check if new code emits metrics: latency_ms/hotpath and cache_hit_ratio. If not, ask author to add minimal metrics.
- Trace spans: ensure token-generation span present and tagged with feature flags or PR id.

Common risky code patterns to flag with examples:
- Synchronous disk reads in request path (e.g., loadConfigFromFile() on each request) -> require caching or background load.
- Global mutable state without locks in concurrent hotloop -> potential race; require explicit synchronization or sharding.
- Large object allocation per token (e.g., new Vector per token) -> object pooling suggested.
- Reintroducing blocking syscall on main thread (dns lookup, auth token fetch) -> use async or background refresh.

Notes on gradation (how I categorize risk quickly):
- LOW: refactors, renames, comments, docs, non-hotpath tests.
- MEDIUM: changes to scheduling, batching thresholds, config exposure (if default unchanged). Require smoke bench.
- HIGH: changes touching token loop, allocator, cross-request caches, network serialization. Block merge without perf + e2e.

Follow-ups / TODOs to add to PR when merging (if merged with canary):
- Add microbench to CI (bench marked flakey -> run nightly).
- Add PR id to trace/span metadata for 48 hours post-deploy.
- Schedule 1-hr post-deploy watch with SRE if canary > 5% traffic.

Questions for author (copy to PR comments area):
- Why this approach vs using existing pooling util (link to pool util)?
- Any expectations for steady-state memory usage? Add numbers to PR description.
- Have you run with an isolated KV workload (cold start) and recorded the tail? If not, add those runs.

Jotted commands & quick snippets:
- baseline run (linux):
  git checkout $BASELINE_COMMIT
  ./tools/hotpath_bench --input fixtures/seq128.json --iters 50 --workers 1 > /tmp/baseline.log
  git checkout $PR_BRANCH
  ./tools/hotpath_bench --input fixtures/seq128.json --iters 50 --workers 1 > /tmp/pr.log
  diffstat: python tools/compare_latency.py /tmp/baseline.log /tmp/pr.log

- quick flame collection (k8s):
  kubectl exec -it deployment/serving-runtime -- /bin/sh -c "perf record -F 99 -g -p 1 -o /tmp/perf.data"
  kubectl cp deployment/serving-runtime:/tmp/perf.data ./perf-pr.data

Misc notes (brain dump):
- If author insists on a change that increases p95 but reduces cost significantly, require an explicit cost/latency tradeoff doc + opt-in flag for customers.
- Remind: Any change that touches quantized kernels needs applied-ml review (link to team).
- Keep this doc lightweight; if a PR triggers many items, convert to a formal runbook and link.

Status: draft — keep adding quick heuristics. If helpful, add a small template PR checklist snippet below for copy/paste.

-- PRI: quick PR checklist snippet (paste into PR description) --
[ ] Hotpath? (yes/no)
[ ] Smoke bench results attached (baseline vs PR)
[ ] Metrics emitted for new code (yes/no)
[ ] Feature flag present (yes/no)
[ ] Rollback steps listed (image tag / flag / revert)
[ ] SRE notified if canary > 5%

End of scratchpad.
